title: Memories of a Good Friday 30 Years Ago
description: I didn’t quite get it together in time to relaunch MarijuanaNews last Friday, but this morning I remembered something that happened on Good Friday ...
content_html_sanitized:
I didn’t quite get it together in time to relaunch MarijuanaNews last Friday, but this morning I remembered something that happened on Good Friday of 1995.

 

I was in the NORML office in Washington, and I took a call from a woman who said that her elderly father was undergoing chemotherapy for cancer and he was vomiting violently, because the pharmaceutical antiemetics had stopped working.

 

One of the nurses whispered that her father had the same problem and marijuana had really helped him, so she asked another nurse who said, “It works for some people.”

 

So naturally she asked the oncologist, who snapped, “It’s illegal and I don’t want to discuss it.” And like Pontius Pilate, he left the room.

 

Then she explained that she had managed to get some marijuana anyway and gave it to her father, and it really worked, and he was doing much better.

 

So I said, “That’s great. How can I help?”

 

She replied she was just concerned that she might give him an “overdose”. I reassured her that there wasn’t a lethal dose, and we chatted a bit more and she told me that she lived near Baltimore, thanked me and said goodbye.

 

After that I realized that where she was calling from was close to where Francis Scott Key wrote America’s National Anthem, which ends with the words, “Land of the Free and Home of the Brave.”

 

And I am still angry.

 

From 1999: New York Times Runs Pro-Medical Marijuana Op-ed By National Review Senior Editor Richard Brookhiser
